the Planck/LFT sidelobes level is very low and that the straylight rejection is excellent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simulation techniques for the radiation pattern prediction of the LFI-Telescope are now fully developed, and the results are in good agreement with the measured data.
we have been able to predict the Planck-LFI antenna pattern in an extremely accurate way, and to evaluate the antenna sidelobes down to -70 dB, with a very high confidence level.
we have developed a new approach to evaluate the radiation pattern of a multi-reflector antenna, which is based on a combination of the GTD methods and the ray tracing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the straylight level of a complex system like Planck/LFI is not dominated by the main reflectors, as it would have been expected.
the straylight rejection performance of the telescope is mainly limited by the feed horns and the feed horn support structure.
a careful analysis of the radiation pattern of the telescope is necessary for a correct interpretation of the data.
